title: Un verre après le tournage  (A Drink After the Shoot)

segments.t: On the film set, Guy Marchand has just finished a deeply moving scene thanks to Arlette's playful suggestion. As the crew prepares the next take, Guy invites his trusted agent to celebrate with a drink after wrapping. Listen to the scene in French first. Don't worry about catching every word.
C'était vraiment très beau.
Et surtout inattendu.
Pour moi aussi, Guy.
Échanger nos rôles sur scène...
C'était juste une blague, je te jure!
On va bientôt commencer la répétition.
Prends ton temps, Guy.
On pourrait prendre un verre après?
D'accord, avec grand plaisir.
Il y a un petit café plus loin.
Vers vingt-deux heures, ça te va?
Ce n'est pas trop tard pour moi.
Alors à tout à l'heure, Arlette.
Let's walk through this warm movie set conversation step by step.
C'était vraiment très beau.
'That was really very beautiful.' Opening with 'it was' is the all-purpose handy chunk you'll use in French after any performance, meal, or trip.
Et surtout inattendu.
'And above all unexpected.' Because 'wait' in French can also mean 'expect', adding 'un-' onto 'waited-for' builds 'unexpected'!
Pour moi aussi, Guy.
'For me too, Guy.' Word for word, 'for me also' matches English order and makes an easy three-word reply in French.
Échanger nos rôles sur scène...
'Swapping our roles on stage...' Notice there is no 'the' at the end: 'on scene' bare means 'on stage' in French, whereas adding 'the' usually means a specific 'scene'!
C'était juste une blague, je te jure!
'It was just a joke, I swear to you!' After the everyday word meaning 'joke', 'I swear to you' — a cousin of English 'jury' — adds lively conversational emphasis.
On va bientôt commencer la répétition.
'We are going to start rehearsal soon.' Built from 'well' plus 'early', French 'soon' tucks right between 'goes' and 'to start' rather than waiting at the end.
Prends ton temps, Guy.
'Take your time, Guy.' Matching English 'take your time' word-for-word, this reassuring expression works in any relaxed conversation.
On pourrait prendre un verre après?
'Could we have a drink afterwards?' Saying 'we could take a glass' softens the invitation politely, and bare 'after' at the end works like 'afterwards' in French.
D'accord, avec grand plaisir.
'All right, with great pleasure.' Just like English, this warm acceptance drops 'a' inside the set expression 'with great pleasure'.
Il y a un petit café plus loin.
'There is a little cafe down the road.' At the end, 'more far' is how French says 'further down the street', right after 'a little cafe'.
Vers vingt-deux heures, ça te va?
'Around ten o'clock, is that good for you?' Two scheduling gems meet here: 'towards twenty-two hours' means 'around ten p.m.', and 'that goes to you?' asks 'does that work for you?'.
Ce n'est pas trop tard pour moi.
'It is not too late for me.' Pairing 'too' and 'late' gives the exact opposite of 'too early' in French, closed off cleanly by 'for me'.
Alors à tout à l'heure, Arlette.

'See you soon then, Arlette.' Placing 'until' ahead of 'all at the hour' builds a farewell you'd use specifically when seeing someone again later the same day! Now let's listen to the whole dialogue again.
C'était vraiment très beau.
Et surtout inattendu.
Pour moi aussi, Guy.
Échanger nos rôles sur scène...
C'était juste une blague, je te jure!
On va bientôt commencer la répétition.
Prends ton temps, Guy.
On pourrait prendre un verre après?
D'accord, avec grand plaisir.
Il y a un petit café plus loin.
Vers vingt-deux heures, ça te va?
Ce n'est pas trop tard pour moi.
Alors à tout à l'heure, Arlette.
After a triumphant scene on set, Guy Marchand invites Arlette out for a drink, celebrating their long friendship and successful collaboration. See you next time!
Bonne soirée!
